agent_notes: The Hebrew verse 1 is the superscription; the KJV counts it as verse 0, so every later verse here is one higher than in the KJV. The commentators' occasion (Radak: David fleeing Saul; Malbim: Keilah and Ziph) is tradition, not text; I mention it only as tradition.

STEPBible glosses נַפְשִׁי as 'being'; here the whole person is meant, so I gloss 'my throat/self' as 'my self'. In the literal layer I keep 'belly' for בֶּטֶן; YLT and BBE soften to 'body'. The verb עָשְׁשָׁה occurs twice (v. 10 and v. 11) and its sense is uncertain: 'waste away, decay' (HALOT) with moth/rot as the traditional link (Radak, Metzudat Zion); Rashi derives it from a glass lens, 'grow dim'. I follow the first and give the second as an alternative.

Revised after review: the claim that the KJV loses the repeated verb is removed. The KJV in fact keeps the echo, 'consumed' for עָשְׁשָׁה in 31:9 and for עָשֵׁשׁוּ in 31:10; YLT ('become old' only in the second) and BBE vary. בַּעֲוֹנִי can mean 'because of my iniquity' or 'through my affliction, the penalty for iniquity'; I keep 'iniquity' and note that the psalm does not say what the wrong was.

agent_notes: YLT renders עָתָק 'ancient sayings'; I follow the majority (arrogant, hard speech: Radak, Metzudat Zion, Rashi's second reading).
The packet's YLT for 31:19 ends mid-sentence and shifts the rest into the next verse; this is a versification difference in YLT only and does not affect the translation.

מֵרֻכְסֵי is uncertain. Rashi reads 'conspiracies/bands' (a binding together), Radak 'pride, heights'; I follow the 'conspiracies' sense in the dramatic layer and flag the alternative in the commentary.
נִגְרַזְתִּי occurs only here. The gloss 'I am cut off' follows Rashi and Radak (from גַּרְזֶן, axe); Rashi also records Menahem's alternative, 'driven out' (cf. Jonah 2:5 נִגְרַשְׁתִּי).

Glosses realigned to the tokens as requested: 10 עַל 'upon', 11 יֶתֶר 'excess (full measure)', 12 עֹשֵׂה 'the one who does', 13 גַאֲוָה 'pride'; no extra '[arrogance]' gloss. Token 5 חֲסִידָיו and token 6 אֱמוּנִים are glossed separately: 'his faithful ones' (the loyal) and 'the trustworthy'.

עַל־יֶתֶר is disputed. Rashi gives three readings: measure for measure (an arrow aimed at the bowstring, yeter), rope against rope, or yeter as a word for pride (cf. Isa 15:7). Ibn Ezra reads 'the remainder of the proud'. I follow the common reading 'to the full, in excess' (Radak, Meiri: on the abundance of their pride), which is also the KJV/ASV 'plentifully'. This is a judgment call.

The New Testament use of this verse (Luke 23:46) is mentioned in the commentary from my own knowledge, not from the packet. The perfect פָּדִיתָה is read as a statement of past rescue that grounds the prayer (so the five English versions agree), though Radak and Meiri take it as a perfect of certainty for the future; I note both.

The Hebrew text reads 'I hate' (שָׂנֵאתִי); some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient versions read 'you hate' (שָׂנֵאתָ). I follow the Masoretic text as given in the packet and do not cite the variant as a source.
